answer: Relic Window Check. Each identity registers the hash of a random historical block as a relic, chosen uniformly from a window published only after registration closes; valid entries must predate the window by a fixed margin. A gale of fake identities cannot precompute matches, so each attempt costs one full registration cycle. Repeated entries face a velvet decay: reuse lowers eligibility for the next epoch, forcing attackers to sustain fresh cycles per identity indefinitely.
